Opportunities for Solar Industrial Process Heat in the United States. NREL/TP-6A20-77760. Golden, CO: National Renewable Energy Laboratory. https://www.nrel.gov/docs/fy21osti/77760.pdf

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 13). The report is a technical-potential study: it contains NO capex, O&M or LCOH figures and no per-technology efficiency table. Loaded: the five solar technology packages of Table 6 (flat plate with water storage, parabolic trough without and with 6 h oil TES, DSG linear Fresnel) with temperature limits (text p.29, Table C-1), field sizes, and design-point efficiencies read from the printed SAM screenshots in Appendix D (loop conversion efficiency for trough no TES and LF; flat plate collector intercept 0.733; the 6 h TES trough has no efficiency printed), plus the PV-coupled electric boiler, PV resistance heating and heat pumps (temperature limits from Table C-1; COP bounds 1-6 from Appendix E). Efficiencies from screenshots are small-print values read from a rendered page: verify. The 6 h TES trough shares the optical collector of the no-TES case. Process temperatures by unit process are NOT in the report (only industry-level totals by temperature band; Table 3 and Table 2 in other-values). Trap: Table C-1 prints LF as "<250-400 degC" while the text limits steam to 300 degC and demand filtering uses <212 degC. Evacuated tube collectors and PVHP are not separate packages with parameters. No price year (no costs).
